The named volume is declared under a top-level volumes: key. R22's letter is met; I flag separately that the port publishes on all interfaces rather than loopback.

The file opens with "# LOCAL DEVELOPMENT ONLY — no credentials." followed by three paragraphs stating that authentication is disabled on purpose, that anyone who can reach the port has full read/write on every database, and that it must never be deployed or copied to an environment reachable from outside the machine.

db:up is `docker compose up -d --wait` — detached, and --wait blocks until the healthcheck reports healthy. NOT EXECUTED BY ME, stated plainly: the Docker daemon is unreachable on this machine and the CLI hangs rather than erroring — I bounded it myself (`docker --version` answers 27.3.1 in <1s, but `docker info`, `docker compose ps` and `pnpm db:up` each had to be SIGKILLed after 10s/10s/25s). So this rests on reading the script plus the Implementer's recorded run (exit 0 in ~6s, `docker compose ps` -> "Up 5 seconds (healthy)").

db:down is `docker compose down` with no -v, so the named volume survives by construction — there is no code path that could remove it. Not executable here (see R24); the Implementer's recorded experiment inserted a document, ran db:down, re-ran db:up and read it back (count=1).

db:reset is `docker compose down -v && docker compose up -d --wait` — the volume is removed, then a fresh container is brought up and waited for. The && means a failed teardown stops the sequence rather than racing a half-reset. Not executable here (see R24); the Implementer recorded countDocuments() -> 0 and getCollectionNames() -> [] afterwards.

All three db:* scripts are bare `docker compose` invocations: no wrapper script, no retry loop, no `|| true`, no output redirection, so Docker's own stderr and exit code reach the shell unchanged by construction. I could not reproduce the failure behaviour: in this machine's half-dead daemon state the CLI hangs instead of returning, so my bounded `pnpm db:up` was killed at 25s rather than exiting non-zero. That the hang happens INSIDE the Docker CLI (a bare `docker info` hangs identically) is itself evidence the script adds no masking layer. The Implementer recorded the clean-shutdown case: Docker's own "Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at unix:///…/docker.sock. Is the docker daemon running?" printed unchanged, exit 1.

Vas a BORRAR todos los datos de la base «memora». ¿Seguro? (y/N)". The prompt is awaited BEFORE cleanDatabase is called, so nothing is touched first.

The implementation is correct — main.ts:116 is `default: false, // Enter cancels (R48).` — and I confirmed the behaviour live: the prompt renders "(y/N)" and pressing Enter resolved to "No" and printed «Operación cancelada: no se ha borrado nada.». But nothing automated asserts it. I probed it twice: flipping main.ts:116 to `default: true` (Enter would delete the database) leaves console-runner 7/7 green, and passing a literal `true` in place of `confirmed` at main.ts:119 — which makes the confirmation pure theatre, deleting even when the human declines — ALSO leaves 7/7 green. The gap sits inside design.md's human-approved "the prompt layer is not tested, by decision", so it is a specified gap rather than an implementer omission; raised as the headline advisory in my verdict with a cheap TTY-free closure.

cleanDatabase calls dropDatabase(client) — which drops the URI-encoded database — and returns { status: 'dropped', database }; main.ts prints «✔ Base de datos «<db>» borrada.». clean-database.spec.ts asserts dropDatabase was called exactly once (toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)). Probed: making client.dropDatabase stop being called turns client.spec.ts red (killed). Not executable against a real server here (no reachable Mongo); the Implementer recorded the real database empty afterwards.

The guard `if (!confirmed) return { status: 'cancelled' };` is the first statement in cleanDatabase, before anything touches the client, and the spec asserts that not even db() was called on the double. Probed twice and both killed: removing the guard outright (1 of 3 red) and inverting it to `if (confirmed)` (3 of 3 red). Reproduced live too — Enter at the confirm printed the cancelled message. This is the data-loss guard and it is genuinely protected by the suite.

The drop is wrapped in try/catch returning { status: 'failed', error } rather than throwing; clean-database.spec.ts drives a rejecting double ("not authorized to execute dropDatabase") and asserts the reported error; main.ts prints «✖ No se pudo borrar la base de datos.» plus the message and continues the loop. Verified the loop survives an operation failure live via the connection-check failure path.

findings.summary: The destructive confirm's `default: false` — the keystroke that separates cancel from delete — has no automated assertion; flipping it to `default: true` leaves console-runner 7/7 green.

Same untested seam, worse mutant: replacing the `confirmed` argument with a literal `true` makes the confirmation pure theatre — declining still drops the database — and the suite stays 7/7 green. The prompt layer's correctness rests entirely on a one-off manual observation that does not regress.

The menu dispatch is an if-chain with no terminal else, so an unrecognised choice would spin the for(;;) loop silently instead of failing loudly. Unreachable today (the value set is a closed typed union), so hardening rather than a bug.

Result assertions use toEqual rather than toStrictEqual in seven places, so an unexpected undefined-valued property would pass: client.spec.ts:39/51/73, clean-database.spec.ts:23/31/44, check-connection.spec.ts:17.

`expect(screen.getByRole(...)).toBeDefined()` is a redundant assertion — getByRole already throws when the element is absent. Cosmetic only: I probed the test and both the greeting and the shadcn Button marker are genuinely load-bearing.

The shadcn aliases `utils` (#/lib/utils) and `hooks` (#/hooks) point at paths that do not exist — apps/web/src/lib and apps/web/src/hooks are both absent, and the package's #/* import map resolves to ./src/*. The next `shadcn add` will generate an import that does not resolve; the components in the tree today take `cn` from the npm package instead.

R48 PARTIAL: implemented correctly and demonstrated live (the prompt renders (y/N) and Enter cancels), but untested — two separate mutants at the prompt layer survive. The gap sits inside design.md's human-approved "the prompt layer is not tested, by decision", so it is a specified gap, not an implementer omission. All other 58 requirements PASS.

R44 covers Ctrl+C only and is satisfied (exit 0, no stack trace, reproduced live). Stdin EOF (Ctrl+D) is unspecified and exits 13 with "Detected unsettled top-level await". Not a compliance failure, but it is absent from progress.md, which R58/R59 make the durable real-run record.

R24-R27 could not be executed in this review: the Docker CLI hangs on this machine rather than erroring (docker info / docker compose ps / pnpm db:up each SIGKILLed after a bounded wait). Verdict rests on reading the scripts — bare `docker compose` calls with no masking layer — plus the Implementer's recorded runs. Stated so the coverage is not overclaimed.

Medium / hardening (§10 data-loss, the declared class for Group 3): `- '27017:27017'` publishes the credential-less MongoDB on 0.0.0.0, so on any shared or untrusted network every host on the LAN gets unauthenticated full read/write on every database — including the dropDatabase this delivery ships. The header comment warns against copying the file to a reachable environment, but the default binding already makes the dev machine reachable. `'127.0.0.1:27017:27017'` closes it while still satisfying R22's port publication and R28's mongodb://localhost:27017/memora.

Low-Medium / hardening (§11 executable surface): the workflow declares no `permissions:` block, and the repository default is default_workflow_permissions "write" with can_approve_pull_request_reviews true — so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN can write to the repository. Its three actions are pinned to mutable major tags (actions/checkout@v7, pnpm/action-setup@v6, actions/setup-node@v7), so a compromised release of any of them would run with a write-scoped token on every same-repo PR. One line fixes it: `permissions:\n  contents: read` on the job. Not a spec violation — R52-R54 say nothing about token scope — so a recommendation, not a block.

Low / informational (§6 dependencies): the shadcn components take `cn` from a third-party npm package rather than a local src/lib/utils.ts. It is a very short package name (typosquat shape) carrying a caret range, and its lockfile entry declares hasBin: true, so it links a binary. Mitigations present: pnpm 10 blocks dependency install scripts by default and pnpm-workspace.yaml re-enables them for only esbuild and lightningcss, so `cn` runs no postinstall; the lockfile pins an integrity hash. Worth pinning exactly, as the rest of the toolchain is.

Low / informational, named per §11 because it is code that runs at install time: `onlyBuiltDependencies: [esbuild, lightningcss]` re-enables dependency build scripts for those two packages. Narrow, deliberate and commented in the file with the reason; no other package regains that privilege.

Checked and clean, recorded so the absence is evidence rather than silence (§4 secrets): the configuration error quotes only the example URI constant, never the resolved value, so a MONGODB_URI carrying credentials is not echoed to the console. No secret, token or PII appears in any log line, .env is gitignored and .env.example holds a placeholder only.

Pass 5 (branch with no default): the menu dispatch has no terminal else, so an unrecognised choice would loop silently rather than fail loudly. Unreachable with today's closed typed union — hardening, not a live bug.

Pass 1, judged COMPLIANT and recorded so the judgement is visible: closeClient's catch is empty, but it carries an explicit comment stating the intent ("closing is best-effort during shutdown: a failure here must not mask the reason we are shutting down"). The skill's rule is that an intentional silent path must say so, and this one does. Every other error path in the change is loud: the config error and both operation failures are printed with the underlying message kept verbatim, and checkConnection/cleanDatabase return explicit failure-shaped results rather than success-shaped ones.

The only logic-bearing file in the change with no dedicated spec — and seven requirements ride on it (R38, R39, R41 wiring, R42 wiring, R44, R47, R48). design.md excludes it by human-approved decision, so the gap is specified; my two surviving mutants are what that decision costs. Cheapest closure without driving a TTY: extract the confirm's options into a `buildCleanConfirm(database)` factory and assert `default === false` and that the message names the database; a second ten-line test could cover the dispatch by extracting the choice handler.

The db:* scripts and the compose manifest have no automated coverage at all, and cannot have any — R56 requires the suite to be hermetic — so R24-R27 rest entirely on the recorded real run. Accepted as a deliberate consequence of a requirement, noted so it is visible rather than implicit.

No gap. Every logic-bearing module except main.ts has a co-located spec covering happy path, error path and an edge case, and I measured their strength rather than counting them: eight of my ten suite-level mutants were killed, the two survivors both landing in main.ts. Coverage of the new behaviour is real, not nominal.
